kjv: shall kill it in the evening
note: ben ha'arbayim is literally "between the two evenings", usually understood as the time between sunset and dark (or late afternoon to sunset); "in the evening" smooths over a phrase whose exact limits were later debated.

kjv: nor sodden at all with water
note: bashel mevushshal means boiled/cooked; "sodden" (old past participle of seethe) now means soaked.
wayyish'alu (sha'al) means they asked or requested; there is no loan, and v.36 calls the result plunder.

kjv: so that they lent unto them
mine: so that they granted what they asked
note: wayyash'ilum (hiphil of sha'al) means "they let them have what they asked"; "lent" implies return, contradicting "they plundered (natsal) the Egyptians".
